title: State Renaming and Action Application
statement: Let $f$ be a function between state sets, let $a$ be a one-step action of a $k$-work-tape Turing machine, and let $c$ be a configuration on a fixed input word. Applying the action after renaming its successor state and the configuration state along $f$ gives the same configuration as applying $a$ to $c$ and then renaming the resulting state along $f$.
hypotheses_covered: A one-step action for $k$ work tapes
A configuration on a fixed input word
replaced:
Let $f$ be an arbitrary function from one state set to another (no
injectivity is required), let $a$ be a one-step action of a Turing machine
with $k$ work tapes, and let $c$ be a configuration on a fixed input word.
Then applying the action $a$ with states renamed along $f$ to the
configuration $c$ with state renamed along $f$ yields the same configuration
as first applying $a$ to $c$ and then renaming the state of the result
along $f$.
